reviews.reason: Even with standard Borel coding and universality of countable linear-order isomorphism allowed, the task must construct an arithmetic distance set with exactly recoverable order information. The two linked bands and three markers, followed by uniform definability of the lower band and its order from the triangle relation, are a substantive original coding argument; ordinary coding prerequisites do not supply it.
reviews.core_assessment: Independently checked all triangle cases and the inverse formulas in902-925. Capped-addition closure follows from2+2=4,2+4=6,2+O being the upper band, and any two values larger than3 summing above6. Triples without2 are automatic triangles. With2 and cross-band elements a and2+b, the triangle condition is exactly b<=a. Only2 satisfies exists y not R(x,x,y); the displayed lower-band formula excludes4 using the final existential and includes every a in O by choosing6. For x,y in O the order formula has witness2+y exactly when x<y. Thus an arbitrary triangle isomorphism, not only the constructed forward map, recovers the order.

Neither the distance-set gadget nor the reverse definability argument is supplied as a free input.

standard_prerequisites.name: Standard Borel coding of countable linear orders and a Borel embedding into the rational interval (3,4)
standard_prerequisites.use: An order on a countable enumerated domain can be embedded by placing successive elements between the finitely many previous images. The choice at each stage uses finitely many order relations; this is the routine coding used by source903/924.

standard_prerequisites.name: Universal S_infinity orbit equivalence relation
standard_prerequisites.statement: E^infinity_{S_infinity} denotes an equivalence relation Borel-universal for isomorphism of countable structures. Isomorphism of countable linear orders is a standard complete example.
standard_prerequisites.use: Only the Consequently sentence of the counted theorem; the triangle encoding is not supplied by this fact.

core_obligations: Encode the order copy O in (3,4) by the distance value set {2,4,6} union O union (2+O), verifying closure under capped addition.
Show any order isomorphism induces a triangle-preserving bijection of the constructed sets.
Recover 2, the lower copy O, and its strict order solely by formulas in the ternary triangle relation, so an arbitrary triangle isomorphism must recover the original order.

proof_roadmap.step: Construct the two bands and fixed markers; extend a linear-order isomorphism.
Define the marker2, identify the lower band, and reconstruct x<y using an upper-band witness.
Use the standard uniform rational-embedding coding to obtain Borelness.

approved_task_config.difficulty_reason: The remaining task is an explicit recoverable coding of arbitrary countable order types into a constrained arithmetic class of distance sets. It requires selecting the three markers and two linked bands so that all nontrivial triangle constraints remember precisely order, and then recovering both the coding domain and its order by uniform first-order formulas. The standard universality of countable linear orders gives no such triangle gadget or converse recovery.

compared.difference: The old item treats normalized unbounded distance sets and concludes equivalence iff equality. This counted theorem concerns bounded positive-infimum sets and codes arbitrary countable linear-order isomorphism into them.
The published pilot is about finite local models for residually finite isometric actions, not triangle-equivalence coding of order isomorphism.
Rado spanning-subgraph equivalence for a nontrivial neighbourhood filter; no triangle-isomorphism coding or scalar rigidity.
Back-and-forth ranks for ordinal powers of integer orders, not triangle equivalence of distance value sets.
Integral separating vector under a triangular matrix action, not coding or rigidity of metric triangles.
Two bounded-component Borel covers obtained from a forward-independent hitting set, not metric triangle equivalence.
The other task imposes infimum0 and proves all isomorphisms scalar; here positive infimum and boundedness permit arbitrary order-isomorphism complexity.
